brief: Describes a sound once as nodes joined by name, then renders it to memory or a file, or plays it.
detail: A node is something the graph does, not an object you hold: Add... calls add a node and make it the output, NameIt labels the last one, and the ...On calls take a label and build after that node. A node may only take inputs that already exist, so a graph cannot loop. Once Prepare, ToSound, ToFile or PlayFor has frozen the graph, no node can be added: the Add... calls then do nothing and LastError says so. The plain form acts and returns nothing; the Q twin returns the graph. ToSound and ToFile render with no audio device; PlayFor is the only method that opens one. The sound has not been heard by a person (UNPERCEIVED): it is checked by frame count, sample rate and peak level, not by listening.
